item.title: Outgoing Rep Chip Roy says the GOP has already 'delivered significantly,' but must 'finish the job'
item.description: Outgoing House Republican Chip Roy of Texas said that while Republicans have "delivered significantly," they still must "finish the job."
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas — who lost the Lone Star State GOP attorney general primary runoff in May and will depart the U.S. House of Representatives when his current term expires — said Republicans have "delivered significantly" but "need to finish the job."

"Well, we've done so much that frankly, it kinda gets lost in a lot of the noise," Roy told Fox News Digital during an interview on Wednesday, pointing to issues such as tax provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed by President Donald Trump last year.

The Texan pointed to the nation's border as the "biggest example" of Republicans' achievements, saying that "we've literally shut down the flow across the border" through enforcing the law.

He also pointed to the passage of the "Laken Riley Act," a measure named after the 22-year-old woman murdered in 2024 by Jose Ibarra, a man who, according to a 2024 statement by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), had previously been "arrested by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)" after illegally entering the U.S., but was "paroled and released for further processing."

Roy said Republicans "need to unite with a singular vision about where we wanna take the country if we wanna be... rewarded in November... and then frankly looking ahead to 2028."

TEXAS MAGA BATTLE ENDS WITH MIDDLETON VICTORY AS CHIP ROY FALLS SHORT IN AG RACE

"Have we done everything we should do? No," Roy said, claiming that "Congress has fallen short" regarding some of what they "should do."

But he still believes the GOP could potentially retain their majorities in both congressional chambers during the midterms.

"I think right now Republicans are staring at barely holding onto the Senate and slightly losing the House, but I still think we can win the House," he said.

The House is now only scheduled to work for several days next week before a lengthy break until after the Nov. 3 elections. Roy indicated that Republicans should get back to work after the midterms "to do our part to finish the job."

"Obviously I'm not campaigning. So I'm thinking a lot about what we could do with another reconciliation package or what we might be able to do in the lame duck or in January, when I'm not in office," he noted.

FENTANYL DEATHS COULD NOW COST DRUG DEALERS THEIR LIVES UNDER NEW GOP PROPOSAL

In a Sunday post on X, Roy wrote, "Government does not fund anything. It takes money from people under force of law and distributes it to other people very inefficiently and usually tyrannically. Child care is unaffordable because government (& corporate cronyism) has made life unaffordable. Stay out."

The New York Times reported last week that the Trump administration is moving to enable some married people with a stay-at-home parent situation to receive a childcare subsidy from a federal program that was meant to help parents who work.

The proposal "creates the option for a new category of care, parent-based child care, that will allow one married parent to receive C.C.D.F. [Child Care and Development Fund] assistance to care for their own child, while a spouse works at least 35 hours per week," the outlet reported, citing a draft document.

Roy said during the interview on Wednesday, "I just don't believe that it's good for the human soul to have the government coming in with a grant and making you dependent on government. I just don't philosophically think that that's freedom. I think freedom, non-dependence, independence is what makes America great."

A White House official said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital on Thursday that the Trump administration "has not announced any such proposal. Until and unless it does, any discussion about potential policies is baseless speculation."

CHIP ROY FIELDS PROPOSAL TO BLOCK PAY AND POWER FOR LONGTIME LAWMAKERS

As for whether he has any interest in running for office again, Roy said the matter is "up to God" and to Texans, adding that he has "a calling for service" and his current focus is on attempting to "solve the big problems for" Americans.

item.title: Nobody wants AI-generated sports commentators, but a pro golf tournament is introducing one anyway
item.description: The New Mexico Open will debut Duff Foreman, an AI-generated golf commentator joining Notah Begay III on a live YouTube broadcast this week.
item.content:encoded:
Golf fans who tune into this week's New Mexico Open broadcast will be introduced to a new commentator by the name of Duff Foreman. He'll join former PGA Tour winner Notah Begay III and well-known broadcaster Ryan Burr on the call, although Foreman won't technically be on site, seeing as how he's not an actual person.

Foreman is believed to be the first-ever AI-generated golf commentator that will be interacting live on-screen alongside human hosts. It is expected that Foreman will jump into unscripted conversations while providing insights and commentary about the play, the golf course, weather, conditions, and the rules of the game throughout nine hours of live coverage.

The very obvious question here is why? Why are we (humans) adding an AI character (not a human) to a golf broadcast? The New Mexico Open may only be a state tournament streamed on YouTube and televised locally, but it is still a professional event with a purse of $137,000 being contested by Sun Country PGA, a section of the PGA of America.

Begay, who will be pulling double duty and teeing it up in the tournament, tried to justify why an AI character is joining the broadcast.

"Golf fans are always looking for a better understanding of what players are thinking and why they make certain decisions," Begay said in a press release shared by tournament organizers. "If Duff Foreman delivers what we’re expecting, he’ll become another voice in the broadcast, helping us explain strategy, analyze swings, consider changing conditions like weather and course setup, and answer questions in real time. I think that kind of conversation could make the game more interesting and enjoyable for viewers."

Begay is right, golf fans are constantly looking for more insights involving the game and how players go about their business during competition. However, his claim that an AI-generated character that was built on a computer is going to deliver a better understanding of what a human is thinking and how said human comes to a decision may be one of the most disingenuous comments ever shared in an official press release, and in the year 2026, that is saying something.

The "conversation" Begay is hopeful to have with the AI commentator will not be "enjoyable for viewers;" it will be universally hated and mocked, just like the rollout of Foreman across social media in the buildup to the event has been.

Foreman has an X account that not only posts nothing but pointless AI slop, but also has a link in the bio section that directs viewers to a YouTube channel called X-Treme Golf. There, you'll find more AI content, such as Foreman playing golf from the summit of Mt. Everest.

Foreman and this 'content' are universally seen as being pointless and disturbingly dystopian, which brings us back to the original question: Why is an AI-generated commentator being added to a golf broadcast?

I think the answer is both wildly complicated and extremely straightforward.

We're living in incredibly bizarre times where everything you look at, it seems AI is grabbing hold of whatever that something is. Whether the impact of AI is having a positive or negative impact varies depending on the situation and the humans being impacted, but AI is here, and it is evolving by the day.

All signs point to AI being a part of our new norm, and the complicated part is that nobody knows what's around the corner, but knows that something is.

This brings us to the straightforwardness of it all.

You – and that 'you' includes golf broadcasts now – can not afford to be the last one to peek around the corner to see what that something is when everyone seems to be fighting to have the first glimpse.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

There isn't a world – at least we should hope there isn't one – where the Duff Foremans of the world will start taking over sports broadcasting booths.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

The New Mexico Open and the PGA of America, however, can now say they were the first to fully integrate an AI commentator into a live golf broadcast.

In this current state of the world, where the words 'first' and 'artificial intelligence' hold real power, building something entirely unnecessary and unwanted can be viewed as a legitimate move on the never-ending chessboard that represents the AI rat race.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: In Dallas, GOP seeks unity on 9/11, Kirk anniversaries
item.description: A conservative shadow convention in Irving, Texas, honored Charlie Kirk and tackled GOP fissures over federal benefits and the party's future.
item.content:encoded:
A shadow conservative convention took place Wednesday just 15 miles west of President Donald Trump's big shindig in Dallas, with Republicans civilly discussing some of the issues causing fissures in the GOP, and seeking unity in the movement.

Both events occurred as the nation prepared to mark two solemn anniversaries, Sept. 10, the day we lost Charlie Kirk, and Sept. 11, the day that nearly 3,000 Americans were killed by Islamist terror.

Forum, as the shadow conference was called, featured speakers like the Claremont Institute's Michael Anton, an architect of President Trump’s immigration policies, and lively debates, such as one over the future of AI between Joe Lonsdale and Joe Allen.

REPUBLICANS HEAD TO DALLAS WITH ONE MISSION: DEFY HISTORY AND WIN BIG

The evening ended with a tribute to Kirk, reminding everyone on the right that they have too much in common to let petty differences divide them.

The biggest division in Dallas this week among Republicans is over the administration’s plan, led by Vice President JD Vance, to allow married stay-at-home moms to receive federal benefits. Traditionalists are calling it socialism, while populists are arguing it makes the most of a system already in place and accusing the other side of obstinance.

Party unity has been an undercurrent all week in Big D, according to Ross Hemminger, president of the Log Cabin Republicans.

"It’s critical, people need to keep their eye on the ball, they need to be completely and totally focused, the president needs a Republican Congress or things are going to go completely off the rails," Hemminger said.

A similar sentiment was sounded by Jack Posobiec, a close friend of Charlie Kirk.

"I know that Charlie held as his North Star the idea of building the coalition and of keeping the coalition together," Posobiec said. "What Charlie understood is, this is an umbrella. We’re all members of the coalition."

Texas Republicans can see firsthand the importance of coming together, after a bruising Senate primary saw state Attorney General Ken Paxton knock out longtime incumbent John Cornyn. Brian, a convention goer in his 40s who works in finance but spent a decade on Capitol Hill before that, said there's no time for bad blood within the party.

"I wish Cornyn had won, I think things would be easier, but he didn’t," Brian said. "The voters chose Ken Paxton and he is our nominee."

The crucial subplot to all the infighting in the GOP – that Republicans in Dallas are seeking to quell – is the battle for the future of the party once President Trump leaves office in January 2029, not just in terms of who the nominee might be, but what the heart and soul of the party will be.

Cara, in her 30s who works in political advertising, said the party has a plethora of potential 2028 candidates.

"I really love JD Vance and I think he is the future, but I like [Sen. Ted] Cruz and [Gov. Ron] DeSantis, too," she said. "Unlike Democrats, we have a lot of great options."

While the ideological divides in the GOP are real, they are nowhere near as polarizing as those facing the Democrats, who have a wing of their party that is literally embracing socialism and crazy ideas like abolishing the Senate.

In fact, the Democrat civil war has grown so vitriolic that, in a shocking move, Pennsylvania Democratic Sen. John Fetterman gave remarks, via video, to the assembled crowd at the Republican convention, spurring more speculation that a party switch could be in his future.

Meanwhile, in the Texas Senate race, Rep. Jasmine Crockett, who lost a bitter primary to James Talarico, still will not appear with, or even endorse, the candidate voters chose.

DEM SENATOR DELIVERS SURPRISE VIDEO AT REPUBLICAN CONVENTION BACKING MCCORMICK

All in all, despite some sniping and nasty remarks between the traditionalists and the New Right, Republicans are in much better shape regarding party unity.

The assassination of Charlie Kirk and 9/11, the former fresh in hearts and minds, and the latter somehow 25 years in past, need to be solid reminders to Republicans across America that whatever disagreements they may have, what they are fighting for is the America that al Qaeda and Kirk’s killer sought to destroy.

Should Republicans triumph in November, there will be plenty of time for policy debates. But unless unity can achieve that victory, all the arguments will be for naught, as victorious Democrats will surely spend two years blocking everything the Trump administration sees to do.

Now is the time to come together, because losing to socialists doesn’t just mean losing an election, it could very well mean losing America as we have known and loved her.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers blasts Danica Patrick for being 'depressed' during their relationship
item.description: Aaron Rodgers fired back at Danica Patrick's "emotionally abusive" claims in a candid interview with Cam Heyward ahead of his final NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Rodgers is going out with a bang.

Entering what he calls his final season in the NFL, the Pittsburgh Steelers QB took aim at former girlfriend, Danica Patrick, this week in a sit-down with teammate Cam Heyward.

"I dated Danica. She had just retired. She was depressed and not fun to be around. But I didn’t leave her because I was trying to be there and be a good partner. Then it was going a certain direction obviously. There was no intimacy; there was nothing," Rodgers said in the second part of the interview, which dropped Thursday morning.

"She tells a story that she was so blindsided and getting left by you, and that he leaves a trail of blood around him. And I’m like, what are you talking about? That’s not what happened."

.

Lord have mercy. Danica Patrick and Aaron Rodgers haven't dated for years, and it's still the most toxic relationship of all time.

Now, a couple important caveats here ...

Danica Patrick is the one who first poked this bear last year, when she went on Sage Steele's podcast and dropped a couple bombs of her own about Aaron Rodgers.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

She called the future Hall of Famer "emotionally abusive," and accused him of leaving a "trail of blood" toward the end of their relationship.

Rodgers pushed back with Heyward, saying the relationship had hit a wall right before COVID hit in 2020.

"I’m buying a house in Malibu and she goes, ‘Do you want to buy it together?’ And I said no. And she said, ‘You know what that means then?’ And I said, ‘Yeah, that’s the way things are going.’ She said, ‘Well, let’s get counseling.’ Then we got counseling. Then COVID hits and we’re stuck together."

AARON RODGERS CLEARS AIR ON 'RACY' DREW ALLAR DM RUMORS ON CAM HEYWARD PODCAST: 'IT'S NOT TRUE'

A lot of 'he said, she said' here with Danica and Aaron Rodgers, which, to be fair, is usually how nasty breakups go. Everyone has their own version of what went wrong, and who was at fault.

Clearly, Patrick blames Rodgers for what she described as a "sudden" end to their relationship in 2020.

"The breakup with Aaron in 2020, because it was sudden," Patrick told Steele when asked about her most painful experience. "It felt like it was my life. So when you live with somebody, it’s your whole life… And because the nature of the relationship was emotionally abusive, so that wore me down to nothing.

"Everything was torn to bits ... I don’t think I’m saying too much earth-shattering stuff after we — there’s been enough out there."

Now that Rogers has reopened the wound, there's even more out there.

"No one cares what they have to say until they say my name," Rodgers continued. "I dated two women who nobody gives a f--- about unless they drop my name — and they like to say their version of the history of what actually happened."

item.title: MLB great Roger Clemens recalls George W Bush's iconic 9/11 World Series first pitch: 'A perfect strike'
item.description: Roger Clemens recalled George W. Bush's bulletproof vest, dress shoes, and Derek Jeter's advice before the iconic World Series first pitch after 9/11.
item.content:encoded:
President George W. Bush was America’s starting pitcher on Oct. 30, 2001.

In the wake of 9/11, the New York Yankees were playing the Arizona Diamondbacks in Game 3 of the World Series, and Bush threw out the first pitch. Roger Clemens, the Yankees’ starting pitcher that night, described the unforgettable moments that led up to Bush’s first pitch.

"I was actually in the bullpen warming up getting ready for the game with my pitching coach Mel Stottlemyre, and I told Mel let’s stop, I want to watch this," Clemens said during a recent appearance on Fox News’ "Fox & Friends."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"We have the best view, the whole stadium is going to light up, 55,000, whatever it was. You could see the snipers on top of the stadium, and he came out and threw a strike in front of the world, not just there at Yankee Stadium. It was for the world to see and it was nothing but spectacular."

Clemens was particularly impressed by Bush’s perfect strike, given the conditions of the mound and the equipment he had on.

"I could only imagine what President Bush was thinking when he was coming out of that dugout, bulletproof vest on. He threw from the top of the mound, and they dressed the mound with some dirt and mixture, and he’s in dress shoes. And so, to even go out there and not slip and be able to kick his leg up, like I said bulletproof vest and windup and throw a perfect strike right down Broadway," Clemens said.

Clemens said he interacted with Bush in the clubhouse and gave the president a hug. The seven-time Cy Young Award winner said Bush was looking for a place to warm up when he received some sage advice from Derek Jeter.

"At the old Yankee Stadium you got to go out the clubhouse door and go to the right about 60-70 yards, and he went down there, and Derek Jeter, pretty well-known story, they had some small talk and Derek told him whatever you do Mr. President, don’t bounce it, you’re in Yankee Stadium, they’ll boo you," Clemens said.

"And I think he got a little nervous then. It was an awesome moment that I know I’ll never forget."

Clemens hopes that America never forgets 9/11 either.

"I can’t believe it’s been 25 years, I hope these kids that weren’t born then, I hope maybe our generation learned about Pearl Harbor that they learn about and keep 9/11 right there in the forefront of their mind," Clemens said.

For the 11-time All-Star, playing baseball during that time was a way to give grieving families and friends a chance to escape for a few hours each night. He recalled the late George Steinbrenner bringing family members and friends of those who were lost to the game.

For the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the New York Mets will play the Yankees on Friday night at Yankee Stadium.

item.title: Fire aboard cargo ship undergoing repairs at busy Chinese port leaves 25 people dead, five more injured
item.description: A cargo ship called the Ocean Melody caught fire during repairs at Qingdao port, killing 25 of the 42 people on board the Liberian-flagged vessel.
item.content:encoded:
A cargo ship docked for repairs at a port on the northeastern coast of China caught fire Thursday, killing at least 25 people who were on board at the time, according to Chinese state media.

The ship was being fixed by Beihai Shipbuilding Co. in the port of Qingdao — one of the country's major shipping hubs — when it caught fire at approximately 11:15 a.m. local time, the Xinhua news agency reported.

A total of 42 people were on the vessel at the time of the blaze, and 12 of them were safely rescued, Xinhua reported. Five others were injured and taken to the hospital, where they are in stable condition.

CARGO SHIP ATTACKED BY SMALL CRAFT NEAR STRAIT OF HORMUZ, UK MARITIME AGENCY SAYS

Photos released by Xinhua identified the ship as the Ocean Melody. The ship-tracking website VesselFinder lists it as sailing under the Liberian flag.

The Associated Press reported that the fire was extinguished at around 2:30 p.m., a little over three hours after it started. Videos online showed plumes of white smoke billowing from the ship.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Chinese authorities have not said what sparked the blaze while the vessel was undergoing repairs.

TIM SHEEHY EXPOSES A 'SCARY' SHIPBUILDING COLLAPSE THAT LEAVES THE US VULNERABLE TO CHINA

China’s President Xi Jinping called for "intensified efforts" to provide support for those who were affected by the fire, Xinhua reported, adding that Premier Li Qiang said "trapped people" needed to be rescued.

Xi also called for ensuring "preventive measures are thoroughly implemented" and "resolutely prevent major and catastrophic accidents."

Beihai Shipbuilding is a subsidiary of the state-owned China State Shipbuilding Corporation, the world's largest shipbuilder. According to the company's website, its primary businesses are shipbuilding and ship repair.

Qingdao, in China's Shandong province, is one of the country's busiest ports and a major center for shipbuilding, shipping and international trade. The port handles millions of containers each year and is home to several large shipyards.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Republican sounds alarm on rising Dem star: 'This guy’s going to be a problem'
item.description: Mike Collins claims Jon Ossoff is using the Georgia Senate race as a Democratic Party springboard for a 2028 presidential run as a DSA candidate.
item.content:encoded:
DALLAS — There’s a rising star in the Democratic Party that is generating buzz for a possible presidential run, but one Republican argues he’s the only thing standing in the way of a future "DSA candidate" in 2028.

Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., is running to unseat Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., in one of the most closely watched contests of this midterm election cycle. Ossoff has sought to nationalize their battle, focusing more on President Donald Trump and leaning into viral clips on social media to sell his message.

But Collins told Fox News Digital during the GOP’s midterm convention that Ossoff’s intentions extended beyond a second term representing the Peach State. Instead, Collins charged that Ossoff is eyeing the White House and using this cycle as a springboard to get there.

TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATE SURVIVES GRUELING RUNOFF, ADVANCES TO HIGH-STAKES SENATE RACE

"This guy is nothing but a trust fund kid who's never had a real job in his life," Collins said. "And at the end of the day, and I think the whole puzzle has been put together now, you can put the pieces of this thing so easy."

"He caters to that far-left base, and at the end of the day, we've got to stop him in Georgia," he continued. "If we don't stop him in Georgia, this guy's going to be a problem for the entire country in 2028."

Those puzzle pieces were scattered throughout his voting record, which Collins said aligned over 90% of the time with Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., through his support of progressives, like former Maine Senate Democratic nominee Graham Platner and Michigan Senate Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed, and because the bulk of his campaign donations are from out-of-state.

'JESUS WAS A RADICAL': PROGRESSIVES INVOKE CHRIST TO SELL LEFT-WING AGENDA ON CAMPAIGN TRAIL

Collins contended that the final piece was when the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) opened their first permanent field office in Atlanta last month. The organization has not endorsed Ossoff.

"That just tells you, yes, Jon Ossoff is really running for president," Collins said. "He's going to be the DSA candidate. He uses Georgia as a platform to raise money."

Ossoff’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

OBAMA STRATEGIST TURNS ON RISING DEM STAR OVER VIRAL TRUMP ATTACK: 'GRATUITOUS AND UNNECESSARY'

He has previously thrown cold water on the notion that he was chasing the White House and told MSNOW last month, "I have zero interest in running for president in 2028, and, frankly, zero interest in the 2028 fantasy football right now."

The first-term senator is considered one of the most vulnerable incumbents on the Democrats’ Senate map this cycle, running in a state that Trump won in 2024 over former Vice President Kamala Harris by nearly three points.

Still, he has gained national attention over the summer for his speeches on the campaign trail, particularly when he needled Trump in a viral social media clip bringing into question his relationship with his executive assistant, Natalie Harp.

"He doesn't want to do the job," Ossoff said. "He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar."

That remark stoked a news cycle and earned him accolades from the likes of Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., who noted that Ossoff was one of the top communicators on the trail when it came to targeting Trump.
